outputs.intro: Four days gives you room to see Zion Canyon, the separate Kolob Canyons area, and the Zion–Mt. Carmel Highway without rushing. I’d keep the last canyon day flexible, since you haven’t picked dates and some activities are seasonal.

days.label: Zion Canyon orientation and museum views

stops.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
stops.note: Start near the South Entrance, pick up a map, and ask rangers about access for your visit. Allow roughly 30 minutes.
stops.why: It gives you a practical starting point before spending time with the canyon.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: Explore the exhibits on Zion’s people and places; the orientation film runs 22 minutes. Allow roughly an hour for the visit.
stops.why: The exhibits add context to the landscapes you’ll see over the next three days.

stops.name: Towers of the Virgin
stops.note: Step outside the museum to take in the dramatic view of the Towers of the Virgin. Allow roughly 25 minutes.
stops.why: This gives the first day a memorable canyon view without committing you to a long hike.

stops.name: Bridge Mountain
stops.note: Look for Bridge Mountain from outside the museum; allow roughly 20 minutes to linger over the view.
stops.why: It’s another named feature you can appreciate while you’re already at the museum.

stops.name: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center
stops.note: Visit in the morning rather than between noon and 1 pm, when the center is closed; ask rangers what access is available that day. Allow roughly 30 minutes.
stops.why: Kolob is a separate part of the park, so local guidance is useful before exploring.

stops.name: Kolob Canyons
stops.note: Give the landscape an unhurried couple of hours, choosing where to stop once you know the day's access conditions. No particular overlook or trail is assumed here.
stops.why: A dedicated day lets you experience this part of Zion rather than treating its visitor center as a quick detour.

stops.name: Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway
stops.note: If you're traveling by vehicle, set aside roughly two hours for a daylight outing with time to pause where stopping is permitted. Check road and tunnel conditions before setting out; vehicle-size restrictions apply on the section between Canyon Junction and the East Entrance.
stops.why: This puts the highway landscape on its own day instead of squeezing it between the two canyon areas.

days.label: An unhurried day in Zion Canyon

stops.name: Zion Canyon
stops.note: Spend a leisurely few hours with the canyon scenery, choosing your route and stopping points after checking access for your dates. This is flexible time to enjoy the canyon, not a promise of a particular trail or viewpoint.
stops.why: After two days in other parts of the park, you can give the main canyon time without rushing to cover ground.

stops.name: Zion Nature Center
stops.note: If your visit is in summer and the center is operating, allow roughly 45 minutes for its interactive exhibits and ranger activities. Otherwise, keep that time for Zion Canyon.
stops.why: It adds a different perspective on Zion’s habitats when your dates make it an option.

narrativeSections.markdown: This sequence separates Kolob Canyons and the highway into their own outings, leaving the final day open for more time in Zion Canyon. I’ve left out Watchman Trail because the NPS lists it as closed pending repairs. The highway day assumes you’ll have a vehicle; if not, that day needs a different plan.
